mechanism_census_method: EXHAUSTIVE census, not a 30-unit sample: bucket populations at current HEAD are small enough (D=2587, M=3635, V=175, X=53, Z=19, all in the 35-book scope) that grouping ALL units by their `evidence` field (the same C1.5 method: family = string before the first ':') gives an exact, not sampled, mechanism distribution -- strictly better evidence than a stratified 30-per-bucket sample would be, since the grouping key is a hard field match, not a judgment call. Individual sampled units were still pulled and read in full (spot-check, ~2 per top mechanism) to confirm the evidence string's claimed meaning actually matches the record content, per the 'field name is not field meaning' hazard.

D.rate_verdict: NO-RATE (MEASURED absence). Both vehicle books' step-cost-ledger.json (epic-3-core-rulebook and epic-4-ultimate-campaign) explicitly record buckets_not_yet_cleared.D with 'no dedicated D-clearing cycle has run' as of the latest committed ledger, and no receipt anywhere in SD-34 closes a D-named mechanism with a timed cycle. This is unchanged at current HEAD (D's population itself did not move).
D.extrapolated_reference_only: Bucket B's measured range (1.667-5.8 units/hour reaching DONE, n=2 measurements, source forward-plan.json/step-cost-ledger.json) is the nearest analog by shape (content needs placing/modelling), giving a purely illustrative 446-1552 hours for 2,587 units. Labeled EXTRAPOLATED-ANALOG, LOW confidence: D's dominant mechanism (class_feature_of_unmodelled_corpus_class, 35.8%) requires modelling a whole class the engine has never seen, which is plausibly harder per-unit than bucket B's 'place a record in an existing table' shape -- this bound could easily be an underestimate.

M.rate_verdict: NO-RATE despite a PROVEN mechanism family. Unlike bucket D, real M-clearing cycles DID run and DID close units -- AT-34-E3-003's 'BASEITEM: chase' (equipment sub-cause, 7 receipts, closures of 1, 31-across-9-books, 5-in-ultimate_campaign, etc., all ingested-magnitude to grounded) and its 'skill_content' cycle (core_rulebook bucket M 1,048 to 972, 76 closed). But NONE of these receipts record commit-to-commit wall time the way the B/C/U cycles in step-cost-ledger.json do, so no units/hour figure can be extracted from them. Both vehicle books' step-cost-ledger.json still lists M under buckets_not_yet_cleared for the same reason (no timed cycle exists to price it from), which is stale on 'has it moved' but accurate on 'is it priced'.
M.extrapolated_reference_only: The proven mechanisms behave like bucket U's shape (one fix closes a whole matching class at once, not a linear per-record cost) more than a linear per-unit rate -- U's 40.28 units/hour (n=2 cycles, both instrument-correction, source step-cost-ledger.json) gives an illustrative 90 hours for 3,635 units IF every M mechanism behaved like U's single largest-class fix, which the actual receipts (closures of 1, 5, 31, 76 units per cycle, not 48-at-once) suggest is optimistic. EXTRAPOLATED-ANALOG, LOW confidence, likely a floor not a realistic estimate.
